notes: Count: 92 new named-person nodes plus four existing anchors (vp18_aja, dasaratha, rama, sita) = 96 distinct named people. Existing Rama-descendant nodes are not redefined. No anonymous Sagara sons or collective descendants are represented as individual people.

Name collisions are branch-scoped: Cañcu’s Vijaya differs from the later Videha Vijaya; the pre-Rāma Viśvasaha differs from the Viśvasaha already in the Rāma-descendant batch; Daśaratha son of Mūlaka differs from Rāma’s father; earlier Videha Kṛti differs from the terminal Kṛti. Khaṭvāṅga/Dilīpa is one person; he is not the earlier Dilīpa son of Aṃśumant.

Satyavrata and Triśaṅku are one person; Saudāsa, Mitrasaha and Kalmāṣapāda are one person; Mūlaka and Nārīkavaca are one person; Khaṭvāṅga and Dilīpa are one person. The Janaka born from Nimi’s body is also named Vaideha and Mithi. Aliases are labels on a single node, not extra people.

The chapter-4 king Janaka identified as Sītā’s father is kept distinct from the chapter-5 Janaka/Mithi and Sīradhvaja because these passages do not explicitly equate them. Sīradhvaja’s ploughshare event is linked to the existing Sītā node, but not encoded as biological or adoptive fatherhood.
Aśmaka is linked biologically to Vasiṣṭha and Madayantī: the text says Saudāsa was childless and requested a son. No biological father claim is made from Saudāsa to Aśmaka.

Rāma’s antecedents are linked through the stated line Khaṭvāṅga/Dilīpa → Dīrghabāhu → Raghu → Aja → Daśaratha → Rāma. Aja, Daśaratha and Rāma use the existing graph anchors. The Bāhu–Sagara branch is followed in chapters 3–4; the separate Nimi/Videha branch is followed in chapter 5.
